security_spec.violation_condition: Linux kernel trap handler or context-switch code that accesses the CLIC hardware-saved stack frame using positive (pre-mandate) offsets or an otherwise non-conforming layout, instead of the now-mandated negative-offset layout (e.g., reading x10 at SP+4 instead of SP-4). This causes the kernel to read/write the wrong register slots when inspecting or modifying the CLIC-pushed context (e.g., failing to correctly advance mepc for ECALL, or restoring wrong register values on return).
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: hardcoded positive stack offsets (e.g., SP+4, SP+8, SP+24, SP+48) in CLIC/smtp trap handling or context-switch paths that should use the mandated negative offsets (SP-4, SP-8, SP-24, SP-48); also any code that treats the CLIC stackframe layout as implementation-defined rather than architecturally fixed.
security_spec.summary: CLIC stack layout changed from recommended to mandated with corrected negative offsets; kernel code accessing hardware-saved CLIC frames with stale positive-offset assumptions will corrupt register save/restore and break ECALL mepc advancement.

findings.finding: The Linux kernel trap handler (handle_exception) performs all register save/restore entirely in software using the pt_regs structure allocated on the kernel stack. No CLIC hardware-saved stack frame is used anywhere in this kernel. All register save offsets are computed via asm-offsets.c macros (PT_RA, PT_GP, PT_T0, PT_SP, PT_EPC, etc.), not hardcoded stack offsets. There is no CLIC hardware push/pop mechanism active or even compiled-in on this kernel tree.
findings.snippet:
SYM_CODE_START(handle_exception)
  ...
  REG_S x1,  PT_RA(sp)
  REG_S x3,  PT_GP(sp)
  REG_S x5,  PT_T0(sp)
  save_from_x6_to_x31

findings.finding: The ECALL-from-U-mode handler correctly advances mepc in software: regs->epc += 4 at line 332. This is the standard software mechanism for skipping past the ECALL instruction after a system call. No CLIC hardware-saved frame offsets are involved, and the epc field in pt_regs is accessed through the standard C struct member, not through hardcoded stack offsets.

All pt_regs field offsets are computed generically via offsetof() and the standard OFFSET()/DEFINE() macros. No hardcoded positive stack offsets (SP+4, SP+8, SP+24, SP+48) exist anywhere. The offsets are derived from the C struct layout, not from any CLIC-specified hardware frame layout. The kernel's pt_regs is a software-defined structure independent of any hardware push/pop mechanism.

The return-from-exception path restores all registers from the software pt_regs structure on the kernel stack, using standard PT_* offsets. No CLIC hardware pop (auto-restore) mechanism is used. The code even clears any dangling LR reservation (line 298-299) before restoring CSR_STATUS and CSR_EPC and executing sret/mret, which is a safe software practice.
findings.snippet:
REG_L a0, PT_STATUS(sp)
restore_userssp s3, a0
REG_L  a2, PT_EPC(sp)
REG_SC x0, a2, PT_EPC(sp)
csrw CSR_STATUS, a0
csrw CSR_EPC, a2

findings.finding: Context switch (__switch_to) saves/restores callee-saved registers through the task_struct->thread structure, not through any hardware-saved stack frame. No CLIC or SMTP push/pop mechanism is involved. All offsets are computed via TASK_THREAD_*_RA macros from asm-offsets.c.
findings.snippet:
REG_S ra,  TASK_THREAD_RA_RA(a3)
REG_S sp,  TASK_THREAD_SP_RA(a3)
REG_S s0,  TASK_THREAD_S0_RA(a3)
...
REG_L s11, TASK_THREAD_S11_RA(a4)
move tp, a1

findings.finding: Boot-time initialization sets up the trap vector (CSR_TVEC) to point to handle_exception, and initializes CSR_SCRATCH to 0. No CLIC configuration or hardware-saved stack frame mechanism is enabled. The PMP setup in M-mode (CONFIG_RISCV_M_MODE) uses standard CSR writes with a temporary trap handler.
findings.snippet:
.Lsetup_trap_vector:
  la a0, handle_exception
  csrw CSR_TVEC, a0
  csrw CSR_SCRATCH, zero
  ret
